newsitem.title: USA: Cohen warns against Russian nuclear deployment.
newsitem.headline: Cohen warns against Russian nuclear deployment.

text.p: Defence Secretary William Cohen said on Wednesday NATO may have to rethink its plans not to station nuclear weapons in new alliance member states if Russia deployed such arms in ex-Soviet republics.

NATO has tried to reassure Russia about its expansion plans by asserting repeatedly that the alliance has "no reason, no plans and no intent" to station nuclear weapons on the territory of new member states.

But Cohen told the Senate Armed Services Committee: "Implicit in that from my perspective is the understanding that Russia would not place nuclear weapons on the territories of the former republics of the Soviet Union."
"And were they to do so this might very well cause NATO to reexamine its 'no plans, no intent, no reason'" position, he said.

Cohen appeared before the panel with Secretary of State Madeleine Albright to launch the Clinton administration's campaign to win support for NATO expansion, which must be ratified by the full U.S. Senate.

Leaders of the existing 16 alliance states are to meet in Madrid in July to formally decide on the alliance's first post-Cold War members. Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are the top contenders but Romania and Slovenia are also under consideration.
